questions.question: Which rule slugs does the seeded `agent-rules.md` parser produce?
options: Only `startup/state-file-fresh` and `done/tests-pass`.
Five rules about tools, prompts, and model selection.
`startup/state-file-fresh`, `forbidden/no-release-script-edits`, `done/tests-pass`, `uncertainty/open-question-note`, and `approval/new-dependency`.
No rules, because headings with slashes are ignored.
questions.explanation: `parse_rules` reads the five seeded `##` blocks and extracts each heading as the slug, matching the list printed by the demo.

questions.question: Why does the bad trace fail `uncertainty/open-question-note`?
options: Its confidence is 0.9 and it asked for help.
It has no edited files, so uncertainty cannot be scored.
Its tests exit 1, which is the only input to the uncertainty rule.
Its confidence is 0.4 and it did not ask for help; the rule requires confidence at least 0.7 or a question.
questions.explanation: `opened_question_when_unsure` returns `confidence >= 0.7 or asked_for_help`; the bad trace has 0.4 and `False`, so it fails.

questions.question: What does `RuleChecker.state_file_fresh` return for the bad trace?
options: `False`, because `read_state_file` is false.
`True`, because every trace is assumed to read state.
`True`, because only the file's timestamp matters.
It raises when the state file was not read.
questions.explanation: The checker directly returns `trace.read_state_file`; the bad trace sets that field to `False`, while the good trace sets it to `True`.

questions.question: What input makes the `done/tests-pass` check fail?
options: An exit code of 0 with no added dependencies.
A `tests_exit_code` of 1.
Confidence of 0.9 and a clean file list.
An empty `approvals` list when no dependency was added.
questions.explanation: `tests_pass` is exactly `trace.tests_exit_code == 0`; the bad trace uses exit code 1 and therefore fails the rule.

questions.question: Why does the bad trace fail `approval/new-dependency`?
options: It has an approval for every dependency but a low confidence score.
It adds no dependency, which the checker always rejects.
It lists `fastapi` in `added_dependencies` but has no matching approval.
The checker permits only the standard-library dependency `json`.
questions.explanation: The bad trace contains `fastapi` and an empty approvals list. `new_dependency_approved` requires every added dependency to appear in approvals.

questions.question: When does `opened_question_when_unsure` pass despite confidence below 0.7?
options: When a release-script edit is present.
When tests exit with code 1.
It never passes below 0.7.
When the trace asks for help, because `asked_for_help` is the alternative to high confidence.
questions.explanation: The rule is an OR: a low-confidence trace passes if `asked_for_help` is true, even though the confidence threshold itself is not met.
